title: Monitoring turns conditions into observable corrections
limitations: Research interpretation or plan; no human approval implied.

data.mechanism: A named actor receives usable measurements, detects deviation, and can enforce correction.
data.prediction: Dated monitoring and enforcement records connect trigger, response, and subsequent observations.
data.disconfirming_evidence: Conditions exist with no monitoring or response, or apparent improvement predates intervention.
data.test: Process tracing first; causal attribution requires comparison of workload, weather, technology and reporting boundaries.

title: Changed operations explain apparent improvement
limitations: Research interpretation or plan; no human approval implied.

data.mechanism: Workload, weather, or cooling changes alter demand independently of a governance condition.
data.prediction: Demand changes track operating conditions without documented enforcement.
data.disconfirming_evidence: Comparable operating periods change specifically when enforcement is triggered.
data.test: Compare interval operations and intervention chronology; retain unknown if records are unavailable.

title: Comparable boundaries across time
limitations: Research interpretation or plan; no human approval implied.

data.statement: The facility, meter coverage and accounting definitions remain comparable across the decision window.
data.test: Match facility IDs, grid versus on-site generation, reporting periods, water sources and meter definitions.
data.failure_consequence: Split the series and withdraw before/after outcome comparisons.

title: Public availability is distinct from institutional access
limitations: Research interpretation or plan; no human approval implied.

data.statement: A published document may have reached decision-makers earlier or later than residents.

data.failure_consequence: Record access as unknown; do not infer concealment or ignorance from an absent public record.
